requirement: Async broker owner handles accepted/partial/final/id-less events
current_evidence: engine.hpp/.cpp + ws_client.hpp/.cpp (P2b-2, 11-09-2026): a reader thread owns each connection's inbound side; every request is a future keyed by its clientMsgId, registered before the send, sent under the one writer lock, awaited outside the execution mutex; a disconnect fails every request in flight at once; the heartbeat is the reader's. test_async_session.cpp against the scripted fake broker (src/tests/fake_broker.hpp, plain loopback transport): two requests in flight resolve independently and out of order (the cancel returns in < 700 ms while the close waits 1.5 s); an answer after its request timed out is journaled unsolicited under the same clientMsgId; an event with nothing in flight is journaled; an id-less error answers the sole pending request but never one of two; a hang-up fails the pending request at once and a reconnect starts a fresh reader; an extra account's auth-family rejection is skipped while a session-level one closes the socket from the reader; the reader heartbeats while idle. The same binary runs under ThreadSanitizer in CI (make tsan). Event journal + POST /events + cpp_events (P2b-1, #882) settle the keeper's UNKNOWN intents from these frames. Partial fills: the first EXECUTION_EVENT echoing the id answers the request and later ones for the same id are journaled — the keeper reconciles exposure from the journal and the position read (entry-ledger.js), not from the reply alone
required_acceptance_evidence: Out-of-order/duplicate/late events and stalled account never corrupt ledger or block unrelated exits
